reviewPolicy.purpose: Acceptance set: 40 model-routed questions, 20 subjects in English and French, written on 2026-10-05 after the corpus repair and before any generation run. None of them is a development case; rubrics are frozen at authoring and never adjusted to an answer.
reviewPolicy.qualityPass: Pass: correct, relevant, covers every mustCover point in substance and stays grounded in the recorded context. Partial: one point missing or an unsupported but harmless detail. Fail: a wrong claim, a mustNotClaim statement, or the question left unanswered. Critical: a fail on a case marked critical, or any claim that could cost funds or access (recovery, exits, finality, backups).
reviewPolicy.independence: Independent of the development cases, not of the project: authored by the same session that repaired the corpus, reviewed locally with model assistance, not by an independent human.

cases.question: When I send 0.3 BTC from a coin worth 1 BTC, what happens to the rest?
mustCover: A transaction input is consumed whole; the remainder comes back as a change output to an address of the same wallet
Input value minus all outputs is the miner fee
The wallet builds change automatically; the user does not manage it by hand
mustNotClaim: that the remainder is lost or paid as fee
that any real transaction of the user was inspected

cases.question: I only have a laptop with 100 GB free. Can I still verify Bitcoin myself?
mustCover: A pruned node validates every block exactly like a full node
It deletes old block data and keeps the headers and the current UTXO set
It cannot serve old blocks to peers or rescan old history without downloading again; disk needs are orders of magnitude that change over time
mustNotClaim: that pruning weakens the node's own validation
a fixed current disk requirement presented as a guaranteed fact

mustNotClaim: that SPV wallets fully validate consensus rules

cases.question: Can I cancel a Bitcoin payment I sent by mistake?

mustNotClaim: that confirmed payments can be reversed

cases.question: My wallet did not mark the transaction as replaceable. Does that mean nobody can replace it?

Signaling improves predictability; neither replacement nor its absence is guaranteed
mustNotClaim: that all replacements universally require opt-in signaling
a current relay fee threshold as a live number

cases.question: If I use a Taproot address, can observers still tell it is a multisig?

mustNotClaim: that Taproot provides full anonymity

cases.question: If the Ark operator disappears tomorrow, are my funds gone?
mustCover: A vTXO holder can start a unilateral exit without the operator, using the exit data the wallet keeps
The exit publishes on-chain transactions, pays fees and waits for confirmations and timelocks before the coins are spendable
Expiry rules and timings depend on the wallet and server version; check them rather than assuming a universal rule
mustNotClaim: that the funds are lost or confiscated when the operator disappears
that exits are instant and unconditional everywhere

cases.question: What can an Ark operator do with my money, and what can it not do?
mustCover: It cannot move funds without the user's signature and cannot prevent a unilateral exit
It can stop cooperating, which makes exits slower and costlier, and it sees the activity it coordinates
Rounds, refreshes and vTXO expiry depend on its cooperation; the key question is which actions need it
mustNotClaim: that the operator is a simple custodian who can spend the funds
a specific version's behaviour as verified fact

cases.question: Can I keep a photo of my recovery phrase in my password manager as a backup?
mustCover: Avoid photos, cloud copies and digital notes; keep the backup offline on paper or metal, protected against loss, theft and damage
Never share it with anyone, including support; no one can recover a lost phrase
An optional passphrase is a separate secret and a separate way to lose funds, not a default recommendation
mustNotClaim: an example recovery phrase presented as real
that any single backup method is risk-free

cases.question: I have 2 of my 3 multisig seeds. Is that enough to recover my coins?
mustCover: A quorum of seeds alone may not reconstruct the wallet: the complete configuration or descriptor with all cosigner public keys, threshold, script policy and derivation paths is needed too
Verify recovery safely in a test, without sending seeds or keys to anyone
Keep backups in separate failure domains
mustNotClaim: that the seeds alone guarantee recovery
a fabricated descriptor or key presented as real
